observations: The direct current failure is real_tool.case_axi_ddr_interface. Its checker reports stale or absent binding between the current source-identity document, exact Vivado export contexts, canonical ordered VCS commands, command authority references, and the executable authorized by the current tool profile. The functional-simulation precondition also lacks parser-verifiable exact_sample_top_module loading evidence.

The latest case_vcs_functional_sim, VCS analyzer, deadlock/AXI checker, multilayer functional, protocol, DDR roundtrip, and board semantic-evidence tools are not_run because case_axi_ddr_interface failed. Therefore there is no current executed board-level value, numeric, liveness, order, AXI, DDR, weight-consumption, or output-frontier result and no justified RTL root candidate.

The supplied VCS diagnosis is historical_only because a live source SHA256 changed and its gate binding is not current. The prior nonterminal execution can define a required failure lesson—capture the raw termination event and runner budgets—but cannot be used as current hardware evidence or as authority for an RTL patch.

Missing board_axi_ddr semantic evidence and downstream not_run reports are consequences of the precondition failure. They are not independent evidence that report writers, AXI logic, runtime loading, pipeline overlap, or the connected kernel are defective.

All operator-leaf and connected single-transformer-layer gates have live hash-validated pass certificates. The current lower_layer_evidence_challenge is no_lower_layer_challenge, so those modules must not be reopened or replayed now.

The connected kernel is certified as an elastic, rate-insensitive, variable-latency token pipeline. Required boundary order and adjacent-stage cross-token overlap must be preserved; unequal stage duration or lack of all-stage same-cycle concurrency is not a defect by itself.

sacg_memory_truth is authoritative and currently lists 15 active contamination barriers: contamination_barrier.0329, .0330, .0331, .0341, .0342, .0343, .0344, .0345, .0346, .0347, .0348, .0349, .0350, .0351, and .0352. Their artifacts remain planning/debug evidence only and cannot be consumed as validated downstream inputs.

sacg_memory_truth also lists six open retries—retry_request.0136, .0140, .0141, .0142, .0143, and .0144—and no open backtrack request for this hierarchy scope. A fresh Stage7 current-source pass is required before those retries and barriers can be reconciled or promotion can occur.

The current Stage8 barriers do not authorize downstream use of prior repair plans or reports. They do not justify bypassing the present bounded repair decision; they remain active until fresh current-stage checker evidence is promoted.
proposed_actions: Reconstruct the board-simulation identity, compile authority, ordered-command references, executable authorization, and exact-top loading proof directly from the current passed board-discovery artifact and exact Vivado exports, without changing any source hash.
Add the missing framework-runner capability to distinguish simulator termination from remote execution-budget termination and to record wall-time/cycle budgets for the exact invocation.

After case_axi_ddr_interface passes, run a current-source targeted VCS replay at the board layer with direct core/lifecycle/ingress/egress/output-frontier monitors and separate AXI/prefetch progress records.

If the replay reports an executed design failure, localize the earliest current-layer causal boundary before proposing any source repair. Do not reopen a lower layer unless that trace explicitly contradicts a named certified invariant.

If the replay completes, execute the remaining board gate DAG and semantic comparison using the immutable target-model reference, frozen numeric policy, and complete DUT-scope weight-consumption proof.
Only after every current board gate passes, audit the fresh evidence and close or supersede the active SACG retry requests and contamination barriers.
risks: Blindly updating a hash field, authority_ref, executable name, or exact_sample_top_module token without deriving it from the current sample-project and Vivado evidence would bypass the checker and could compile a substitute design.
Changing wrapper, simulation-source, checkpoint, stimulus, target reference, semantic testbench, or numeric-policy hashes would invalidate the repair comparison and lower-layer continuity evidence.

A remote runner timeout or external kill can masquerade as a DUT liveness failure. Conversely, independent AXI/prefetch progress does not prove output or lifecycle-frontier progress; the current run must record both separately.

A board output-frontier stall alone cannot reopen the connected kernel. Reopening it without direct core start, ingress, egress, named-boundary, and current-certificate contradiction evidence would violate the hierarchical repair loop.

Board functional closure can produce a false pass if expected outputs do not come from the real target model on the same immutable checkpoint and stimulus, or if the complete Transformer-block tensor catalog is not tied to executed loader and DUT-consumption hashes.

Shape, tensor layout, token order, DDR address map, transfer count, runtime ABI, and numeric comparison may disagree across artifacts even after the identity precondition is repaired; the ordered board gate DAG must check each rather than infer closure from simulation completion.
Historical contaminated reports or stale diagnosis paths could be accidentally promoted if SACG retry and contamination records are not explicitly reconciled after a fresh pass.

constraints: Do not modify golden outputs, derive expected values from RTL, or loosen the frozen numeric policy.
Keep checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, semantic testbench contract, and exact board-wrapper/source hashes immutable during this repair loop.
Use the exact user-supplied sample-project wrapper and Vivado export facts; do not substitute a simplified AXI/DDR wrapper or guess a top or executable.
Transformer blocks are the complete DUT scope; embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, and sampling remain excluded.
Do not reopen operator leaves or the connected kernel without a current trace binding direct core start, ingress, egress, a named causal boundary, and the current certificate hash.
Preserve the connected kernel's certified elastic variable-latency token-pipeline ordering and cross-token overlap semantics; same-cycle stage start/end is not required.
